ticket.title: A task scoped to a repository with a configured chain was verified by the cargo-test fallback
ticket.description:
Found while verifying CO-10. The task is scoped to repo common with crate gaugeblock-contracts. The suite config HAS a chain keyed common, and the lookup order is crate, then repo, then default - so the repo key should have matched and run fmt/clippy/nextest/audit/docs. Instead the receipt says: no verification command configured for gaugeblock-contracts; falling back to cargo test, verifier storypole-verify:cargo-test-fallback.

So a ticket whose repository has a configured chain was certified by a weaker one. The receipt is honest about it - the warning exists and the verifier name differs - which is the good part and the reason this is a P2 rather than a P1: nothing is lying. But a weaker certification than the configuration promises is exactly the shape GB-272 and SP-29 were about, and it appeared for a ticket scoped to a repository that is in the list.

Worth checking: whether the repo lookup uses the task scope.repo value or derives a name from the checkout directory, whether the common entry is keyed exactly common, and whether the receipt should refuse rather than fall back when a repository key exists but did not match - falling back silently is how a member chain came to run harness commands once before (SP-29).

DIAGNOSED 2026-11-08. The lookup order is not the defect; the configuration source is.

Evidence:
  suite root .gaugeblock/config.toml   -> verification_commands present, 17 chain keys, including "common"
  common/.gaugeblock/config.toml       -> the verification_commands key is absent entirely

When a task scoped to a member repository is verified, the store loads THAT repository's config. The chains are
declared once at the suite root, so a member store asks its own file for a chain keyed "common" (or for `default`),
finds neither, and correctly falls back to `cargo test`. The crate-then-repo-then-default order never reached a chain
because there was no chain to reach. The receipt's warning was accurate: "no verification command configured for
gaugeblock-contracts" is literally true for the config the store was holding.

WHY THE FALLBACK IS THE RIGHT BEHAVIOUR AND STILL THE WRONG ANSWER: falling back keeps a member's verify from silently
running harness commands (SP-29), so the guard is doing its job. What is missing is inheritance - a member store should
consult the suite config for a chain when its own config declares none, because the suite declares membership and the
chains are keyed by the directory names membership uses (ADR 0008).

PROPOSED FIX, not implemented here because it changes config resolution and needs its own tests: in the store's chain
lookup, when the local config yields nothing, retry against the suite root's config before giving up. The receipt should
name which file the chain came from, so `chain_key` answers "which chain ran" and a new field answers "declared where".
That distinction is what made this ticket hard to see: the receipt said which chain did not run, not which file was
consulted.

SECOND QUESTION FROM THE TICKET, ANSWERED: the repo lookup uses `task.scope.repo` directly, and its value here is
exactly "common", matching the suite key. No normalisation defect.

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN, SITES IDENTIFIED, deliberately not started 2026-11-08. The diagnosis above is complete; what
remains is two repositories and a test, and a config-resolution change is not something to land half-verified at the end
of a session.

1. common: `SuiteConfig` exposes `section`, `string`, `boolean` but not an arbitrary top-level key, and the chains live
   at the top level as `verification_commands = [["key", "command"], ...]`. Add `pub fn raw(&self, key: &str) ->
   Option<&toml::Value>` and parse the array-of-pairs in storypole. Parsing stays in storypole for the reason
   suite_config's own doc gives: the foundation crate loads, the tool interprets.

2. storypole-core: `StorypoleConfig` needs the adopted chains plus a record of where they came from. `chain_key` answers
   "which chain ran"; the missing field is "declared where". Without it the next reader repeats this diagnosis.

3. storypole-core/src/store/mod.rs, BOTH construction sites - `open` at lines 69-76 and `open_exact` at 95-102, which
   carry identical three-branch config loading. After the config is loaded: if `verification_commands` is empty, ask
   `gaugeblock_workspace::Membership::containing(root_dir)` for the suite root and adopt its `verification_commands`.
   storypole-core already depends on gaugeblock-workspace, so no new edge is created and the audit rule holds.

4. Tests, at minimum: a member store whose own config has no chains gets the suite's chain for its own directory name; a
   member whose config DOES declare chains keeps them (the suite never overrides a local declaration); a lone checkout
   with no suite behaves exactly as today; and a task scoped to a repository with a chain no longer records
   `storypole-verify:cargo-test-fallback`.

The fourth test is the one that actually closes this ticket, because it is the receipt the ticket was filed about.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-11-08 (d8ad392), end-to-end proof still owed, plus a new inconsistency discovered while looking for it.

WHAT IS PROVEN: `StorypoleConfig::inheriting` is all-or-nothing and three tests pin it - a repository with no chains
inherits the suite's, one that declares chains keeps all of them and gains none, and a lone checkout is unchanged. 162
tests pass, clippy clean. Both store construction sites inherit, so `open` and `open_exact` cannot disagree about a
task's chains.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: a real receipt. The proof this ticket wants is a `common`-scoped verify whose receipt names the
suite's chain instead of `storypole-verify:cargo-test-fallback`, and that needs a full verify run.

NEW FINDING WHILE LOOKING FOR THE PROOF: `storypole config check --dir common` still prints "verification_commands is
empty, so storypole verify falls back to cargo test". It reads the config file directly rather than through a store, so
it does not inherit - which means the audit now contradicts the behaviour it audits. A repository can have a chain that
`verify` will use and an audit that says it has none. Either the audit should report inherited chains (and say where
they came from) or it should describe itself as reporting the file rather than the effective configuration. Leaving the
two disagreeing is worse than either.

That is a second instance of the same shape as this bug: a reader that looks at the file and calls it the truth.

PROVEN END TO END 2026-11-08. `storypole verify CO-1` run from common/ now records verifier `storypole-verify` and
chain_key `common` - the suite's fmt+clippy+nextest+audit+docs chain, not the cargo-test fallback. The ticket file holds
both receipts side by side, which is the cleanest before/after this epic produced:
  before: chain_key null     verifier storypole-verify:cargo-test-fallback
  after:  chain_key "common" verifier storypole-verify

THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS PROOF FAILED, and that is the part worth reading. d8ad392 implemented inheritance and passed
162 tests, and the verify still fell back, because `verification_commands` lives under `[storypole]` in the suite config
and the helper asked the ROOT table for it. Nothing inherited, nothing warned, and the unit tests could not see it: they
tested `inheriting` and never the parse. Fixed in b3fa899.

That is the same defect this ticket was filed about, reproduced inside its own fix - a reader that looks one level off
from where the truth lives and reports absence. Two instances in one ticket, four in the arc.

STILL OPEN, found while looking: `storypole config check` reads the config file directly and does not inherit, so it
still warns that verification_commands is empty for a repository whose verify now uses the suite's chain. The audit and
the verifier disagree, and one of them should say which it is reporting.
